children: According to Sina Finance, Libya’s National Oil Corporation (NOC) said an armed group’s blockade of the Hamada oil pipeline caused losses exceeding $30.7 million. The pipeline connects the Hamada oil field with the country’s largest refinery, Zawiya. The blockade lasted more than 20 days, resulting in a crude oil production cut of 302,778 barrels, valued at more than $30.7 million. The shutdown also caused average daily losses of 14,418 barrels and daily revenue losses of $1,470,636; operating costs at affected oil fields added further losses.

The NOC condemned damage to oil infrastructure, saying such actions harm Libya’s oil industry and its people as the company works to regain the trust of international energy companies and attract investment to increase production. It called on the relevant authorities and the public to take responsibility, restore passage through the pipeline valves and stop encroachments on oil facilities.
On October 30, the NOC reported that an armed group had closed a valve on the Hamada pipeline in the Raya'ina area, sharply increasing pipeline pressure and forcing crude oil shipments to stop.

title: Libya Pipeline Blockade Causes More Than $30.7 Million in Losses
